title: The iron centre of haem
caption: In haemoglobin, Fe²⁺ sits in an octahedral site: four nitrogens of the flat porphyrin ring, one histidine nitrogen below, and O₂ bound above. Carbon monoxide binds the same site about 200 times more strongly, which is why it is poisonous.
alt: An octahedral iron ion with four porphyrin nitrogens around it, histidine below and O₂ above.
description: Four N of the porphyrin in the equatorial plane.
O₂ above, in the sixth position.
